differences.title: 1. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Client asks for exact data needed in one single HTTP request.
differences.rightDesc: Requires multiple roundtrips to different endpoints for related resources.

differences.title: 2. OVERFETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Never downloads unwanted attributes or nested fields.
differences.rightDesc: Server determines payload size, frequently transferring unnecessary data.

differences.title: 3. SCHEMA & TYPING
differences.leftDesc: Strongly typed schema guarantees contract safety between frontend and backend.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on OpenAPI or manual docs without runtime type enforcement.

differences.title: 4. CACHING
differences.leftDesc: Complex POST queries bypass standard HTTP/CDN edge caching layers.
differences.rightDesc: Leverages standard HTTP status codes, ETags, and edge CDN caches natively.

differences.title: 5. VERSIONING
differences.leftDesc: Deprecate fields at granular level without creating breaking API revisions.
differences.rightDesc: Requires major version routing like /v1, /v2 for breaking structural updates.

differences.title: 6. REALTIME UPDATES
differences.leftDesc: Native WebSocket subscriptions stream live events out of the box.
differences.rightDesc: Requires auxiliary protocols like WebSockets or SSE architecture.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires query parser, resolver optimization, and N+1 query protection.
differences.rightDesc: Straightforward controllers, universally understood across all tech stacks.
